answer: Multipath radio fingerprinting counters Sybil attacks in an ecological lagoon. Each node broadcasts pulse trains through an anchored cedar trellis, letting receivers verify the unique spatial multipath profile of its transmitter. Forging identities requires deploying separate transceivers at distinct coordinates, imposing real hardware manufacturing and siting costs per agent. However, wind-driven surface chop on the lagoon causes phase drift that occasionally triggers false rejections.
